speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) what is the implementation roadmap and timeline for the full Open Electricity Market to all households islandwide.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question is: I understand that there are about 26 licensed retailers of electricity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The third question is that we understand that EMA has committed to making switching over easy for consumers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For example, I assume that consumers will have to change their meter boxes, so who is going to pay for that?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The fourth question is the Minister earlier said that we are having a pilot so that we can also study how it pans out.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And if there are any feedback from the pilot, we can fine-tune for the rest of the island.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to ask whether the Government anticipate certain specific challenges from the pilot and whether there is a possibility that such challenges and fine-tuning may set the timeline back to beyond 2018 for the rest of the island?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This may be done by the vendors themselves, for instance.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In some of these countries, the regulator actually takes on the role of accrediting whether that information is accurate, to ensure that the consumers are not duped or given inaccurate information.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: So, could Members keep their supplementary questions short?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I was heeding your advice and that is why I kept my initial answer short to allow for supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There is five, then we try and do justice to some of them, at least.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The pilot in Jurong, does that mean that we will have staggered implementation across the board.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That is exactly why we are having a pilot because we need to understand.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that, I think, would enable the key entities – EMA, SP and the retailers – to also understand if there are any unanticipated challenges.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is precisely that they are unanticipated that I cannot tell the Member, in answer to her fourth question, do we anticipate any specific challenges.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If, however, there are reasons to review that, then we will do so, and we will convey that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The most important point here is the customer experience has to be a good one, and we want to avoid having undue disruption or concern amongst our consumers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, that is our priority in this exercise.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: EMA is now in the process of vetting and qualifying them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They are applying a fairly tight set of criteria.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And therefore, there is a need to make sure that there is an appropriate set of rules governing their conduct and capabilities that the retailers are able to meet.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, this is a process that EMA is going through now in its engagement with the retailers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Before we start a pilot, it should be quite apparent how many and the identity of these retailers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Again, this is something that will be elaborated.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But, essentially, the way the Open Electricity Market is designed − I do not want to get into a very technical discussion − it means you can do a switch without having to have what they call "smart meters" or "advanced meters".

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is possible and, in fact, our system is designed to do that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is based on a principle called "load profiling" instead.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: However, if you have advanced metering infrastructure, it allows for greater flexibility and the kind of plans.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the commercial market, in general, when they opted to become contestable and sign up with retailers, they have had some advanced meters installed.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the case of households, it depends because if their consumption levels are not very high, it may not merit that kind of investment.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the other hand, advanced meters do provide a lot more data which can be very useful for both policy and for system optimisation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we have to work out the trade-offs and design.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Currently, they are replacing the meter outside the houses.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: In Hougang, I saw them changing from a big one to a very small one.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I do not know about the specific meters in Hougang.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I would say that, in general, the replacement for households has not been about going towards smart meters.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Indeed, when you deploy smart meters, you also need to have some backend systems that are able to use them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Otherwise, it is effectively a dumb meter because it does not do much more than a conventional analogue meter.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, this is something that we are studying.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would say that, most likely, it is not, because there has been no plan to implement advanced metering for households.
